title: Friction & Spice — A Journey Through the Depths of Cosmic
paragraphs: Rarely in this ever morphing world of electronic beats has there been an ascension to success as sweet and quick as that of Jeff Alderson and Scott Dixon. Too often, rookie artists release their first tracks which quickly become dance anthems, only to fade away in musical quality throughout their many releases after.

Enter Friction and Spice, a duo of DJ’s who questionably have become the largest name in the southeastern music circuit in the past year. From their first release, Gruv Me, in January 1996, to their latest, The Rhythm, in January 1997, the past year has been nothing but the top scene for them. To put it metaphorically, these kids are running shit like diareah.

The beauty of the entire equation is the amount of time it took them to become a success. In October of 95, Scott Dixon(Friction) took out a six thousand dollar loan to fulfill the dreams of making music. Two short months later, at the start of the new year, Friction and Spice released Gruve Me, which became an instant dancefloor hit. From the melodic piano breakdown, to the analogue bass which tears underneath the Funky break, Gruv Me proclaimed Friction and Spice’s foothold into the music scene. In February, while their first track was still in regular rotation, the duo released Pure, a darker side to their fresh new sound. Track after track, a total of eight records were released in 1996...and many more planned soon after. In this business of one hit wonders, Friction and Spice plan to stay around quite a bit longer. As Spice put it, “You have to do the business 110% for you to be successful.” In all aspects, that’s exactly what they have done.

Don’t be deceived by the short time they have been producing tracks; The two aren’t newbies to the world of music. As many musician do, Friction got his start at a young age spinning Hip Hop. He even had to get a work permit at age thirteen to spin at a club in Virginia. Days progressed as did his skills. Friction expresses that his family is a major aspect in his motivation, “We all have an ambition to succeed”, he says.

As for Spice, the business head of Cosmic records, was born in D.C., raised in Virginia, and has been living in Florida for the past seven years. Like many, he remembers going to Brassy’s and hearing Andy Hughes spin back in the day. As he became turned on to this music, Spice traveled back up to Virginia and threw a total of 70 parties. Starting off small, the parties eventually grew from black and white flyers to full color on A&A graphics.

Before producing music, Jeff and Scott were and are DJ’s. Although both DJ’s claim their own flavor- it can be justified that the style of music they spin simply cannot be touched, or even moreso, categorized. I had the pleasure of spinning with them at the Edge in Fort Lauderdale (As we sat and talked about that night, we decided to shamelessly plug the club and thank Mike Sharpe and Icey; it was Phat!), and the music layed down in the early morning hours epitomized the word darkness. Track after track, Friction slammed the crowd with aggressive beats, or, as he put it, “full-on energy”. Spice went on after, dropping a continual dose of tracks onto the crowd with his style of intelligent breakbeat. As DJ’s, their skills parallel the quality of music they make.

Ask Sasha; he knows of F&S. Trikster is going to be the first release on Sasha’s new label. Friction and Spice have licensed countless tracks to everyone from Sasha to Splash. Before you even get this magazine the release of a remix L.P. will be in the stores. Also, just released off of Duece records is a track by Rich Rosario and Friction under the name Aria.

As for the past, they have already paved their way into a respected position in the music industry. As for the future...who knows? I mean, if they have accomplished so much in so little time, it not only shows devotion, but also the ambition to achieve. And if that’s how’s its gonna be, then you’ve got my vote that they’ll do it.
